sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

Task A1 — build the dense-reference experiment package for Lab 3.

Read predictions.md section "Part A" first. Everything in A.1 is FROZEN: splits, architectures,
optimizers, epochs, early-stopping rule, seeds, thread counts, latency protocol. Implement it
exactly; if something in it is impossible, stop and say so instead of changing it.

Environment: this is a uv project. Run everything with `uv run ...`; add dependencies only with
`uv add`. CPU only. Do not use pip directly.

Build:
1. A Python package in code/lab3/ with a CLI: `uv run python -m lab3 <cmd> --model {mlp,cnn,gcn} ...`
   commands: `make-splits`, `train`, `eval`, `bench`. Configs in configs/<model>.yaml hold the
   frozen hyperparameters; the CLI reads them (flags may override only for tests).
2. Data: download Fashion-MNIST (torchvision) and Cora (torch_geometric Planetoid, public split)
   into data/ (gitignored, not submitted). `make-splits` writes splits/fmnist_{train,val,test}_idx.npy,
   splits/cora_{train,val,test}_idx.npy and splits/SPLITS.sha256. Every other command loads these
   files and verifies the hash; it must never regenerate splits.
3. Models exactly as in the predictions.md table (no BatchNorm). GCN uses torch_geometric GCNConv.
4. Training with validation-selected checkpointing and the frozen early-stopping rule. Save
   checkpoints/dense/<model>_seed<k>.pt (state_dict + metadata), and per-epoch learning curves
   to results/curves/<run_id>.csv.
5. Logging: append one JSON line per attempted run (including crashes) to results/runs.jsonl
   with a unique run_id (e.g. <model>-<method>-<timestamp>-<shortuuid>) and at least these fields:
   run_id, status (ok/failed + reason), part, architecture, method ("dense"), target_sparsity,
   achieved_sparsity, stored_precision, compute_precision, accumulator_precision, seed,
   train_epochs, finetune_epochs, best_epoch, val_acc, val_loss, test_acc, total_params,
   nonzero_params, dense_bytes, compressed_bytes, est_macs, peak_rss_bytes, latency fields
   (median_ms, iqr_ms, warmup, iters, threads, batch_size or "full_graph"), wall_time_s,
   git-free code hash (sha256 of code/ files), torch/python/numpy versions, timestamp, command.
   Never rewrite or delete existing lines.
6. `bench`: latency per the frozen protocol (inference_mode, eval, 20 warm-up, 200 timed,
   median + IQR, batch 1 and 256 for fmnist, full graph for cora), peak RSS measured in a fresh
   subprocess. MAC estimate: analytical per layer (document the GCN counting convention).
7. Tests in tests/ (pytest, `uv run pytest -q`):
   a. tiny-overfit test per architecture (MLP/CNN: 64 training images to >= 99% train acc;
      GCN: train nodes to >= 99% train acc) — a test may use its own lr/epochs, but must not
      edit configs/;
   b. parameter-count test asserting MLP=235146, CNN=117066, GCN=23063;
   c. evaluation never updates weights: state_dict bit-identical and optimizer untouched after
      `eval` and after `bench`;
   d. split files load, hashes match, splits are disjoint, fmnist val is 500/class.
8. After tests pass: run make-splits, then train dense seed 0 for all three models, then seeds
   1, 2, 3 (replicas), then bench each seed-0 checkpoint. Then write results/baselines.md (a table
   of val/test acc, params, bytes, MACs, latency) and figures/learning_curves.png.

Rules: do not weaken a test to make it pass. If a baseline misses its target (MLP>=82, CNN>=87,
GCN>=65 test acc), stop and report a diagnosis; do not change hyperparameters on your own.
Report at the end: files created, test output, the baseline table, and any anomalies.

# Lab 3 — Predictions and Frozen Design Decisions

Each section is dated and was written **before** the runs it governs. Sections are
append-only: later corrections are added as dated amendments, never by editing a frozen
section.

---

## Part A — Dense reference models (frozen 2026-11-09, before any training)

### A.1 Frozen design

**Hardware / software.** Apple M4 Pro (12 CPU cores), 24 GB RAM, macOS. Python 3.12,
PyTorch 2.15.0, torchvision 0.29.2, torch_geometric 2.8.1, NumPy 2.5.4. Package
management with `uv` (`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`). **CPU only for every arm**; no MPS.

**Threads.** `torch.set_num_threads(4)` and `torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)` for all
training, evaluation, and benchmarking.

**Data splits (created once, saved to `splits/`, reused by every arm).**
- Fashion-MNIST: official 60k train / 10k test. From the 60k train set, a stratified
  5,000-image validation set (500 per class) is drawn once with split seed 12345; the
  remaining 55,000 images are the training set. The 10k official test set is the test set.
  Saved as index files plus a SHA-256 of the index arrays.
- Cora: the standard Planetoid public split (140 train / 500 val / 1000 test nodes), saved
  as node-index files with a SHA-256. The graph (2,708 nodes, 10,556 directed edges) is
  never modified by any compression arm.
- Inputs: Fashion-MNIST normalized with mean/std computed on the 55k training split only.
  Cora features row-normalized (standard GCN preprocessing).

**Architectures.**
| Model | Definition | Params (computed) |
|---|---|---|
| MLP | 784→256→128→10, ReLU, no dropout | 235,146 |
| CNN | Conv(1→16, 5×5, pad 2)→ReLU→MaxPool2 → Conv(16→32, 5×5)→ReLU→MaxPool2 → FC(800→128)→ReLU → FC(128→10) | 117,066 |
| GCN | GCNConv(1433→16)→ReLU→Dropout(0.5) → GCNConv(16→7) | 23,063 |

No BatchNorm anywhere (keeps INT8 conversion and structured surgery unambiguous).

**Training.**
- MLP and CNN: Adam, lr 1e-3, weight decay 0, batch size 128, cross-entropy, max **30
  epochs**.
- GCN: Adam, lr 0.01, weight decay 5e-4, full-batch, cross-entropy on the 140 train nodes,
  max **300 epochs**.

**Early stopping / checkpoint selection (validation only).** After each epoch, evaluate
validation accuracy. Keep the checkpoint with the highest validation accuracy; ties go to
the lower validation loss, then to the earlier epoch. Stop when validation accuracy has not
improved for **5 epochs** (MLP, CNN) or **50 epochs** (GCN), or at the max epoch count. The
test set is evaluated only on the selected checkpoint and never feeds back into any choice.

**Seeds.** Each run sets Python `random`, NumPy, and PyTorch seeds to the run seed and logs
it.
- Pilot seed: **0**. Produces the canonical dense checkpoint per architecture. Every
  compression arm starts from it, and the full Part B pilot matrix uses it.
- Confirmatory seeds: **1, 2, 3**. Used (a) to train three replica dense baselines per
  architecture, which report seed variance only and are never used as compression parents,
  and (b) in Part B to repeat the selected operating points. There the seed controls
  fine-tuning shuffle order and dropout, and the parent is always the canonical seed-0
  checkpoint.
- The split seed 12345 is separate from these and is never changed.

**Sanity targets (test accuracy).** MLP ≥ 82%, CNN ≥ 87%, GCN ≥ 65%. A miss is diagnosed,
and the cause is recorded. The target is not lowered.

**Latency protocol.** `torch.inference_mode()`, model in `eval()`. 20 warm-up and 200
timed iterations, timed with `time.perf_counter_ns`. Report the median and IQR. Batch sizes
are **1** and **256** for Fashion-MNIST, and one full-graph forward pass for Cora. Peak RSS
is measured in a fresh subprocess per benchmark.

**Stopping rule for agent work.** If a baseline misses its target after one diagnosed fix,
or any required test fails twice after a fix, work stops and the issue is reviewed before
continuing. Tests are never weakened to pass.

### A.2 Predictions

**Parameter count: MLP (235k) > CNN (117k) > GCN (23k).**
*Mechanism:* the MLP's first layer alone (784×256 ≈ 201k) dominates its count. The CNN
shares 5×5 kernels across positions, so its convolutions are tiny (≈13k), and most of its
parameters sit in FC(800→128) (≈103k). The GCN has a 16-wide hidden layer, so nearly all
of its parameters are the 1433×16 input projection.

**Dense checkpoint size: MLP (~0.94 MB) > CNN (~0.47 MB) > GCN (~0.09 MB).**
*Mechanism:* FP32 state dicts are about 4 bytes × params, plus a few KB of pickle/zip
overhead. The overhead is proportionally largest for the GCN, so its ratio to the others
will be slightly above the raw parameter ratio. The Cora graph is data, not checkpoint.

**Training time to the selected checkpoint: CNN > MLP > GCN.**
*Mechanism:* per image, the CNN does about 1.7M MACs (conv2 alone is about 1.28M), against
0.235M for the MLP. That is about 7× more compute over the same 55k images per epoch,
partly offset by better-optimized conv kernels. The GCN trains full-batch on 2,708 nodes.
Each epoch is one sparse aggregation plus a 2708×1433×16 projection, so 300 epochs should
take seconds, against minutes for the image models.

**Sensitivity to compression (most to least): GCN > CNN > MLP.**
*Mechanism:*
- *GCN:* it has a 16-dimensional bottleneck and only 140 labelled nodes for fine-tuning.
  Every remaining weight carries a large share of the representation, and recovery data is
  scarce. Most of its input-projection weights belong to rare bag-of-words features, so
  moderate unstructured sparsity should be tolerated. At high sparsity, and for structured

moderate unstructured sparsity should be tolerated. At high sparsity, and for structured
  removal of hidden features, I expect the sharpest collapse.
- *CNN:* convolution weights are reused at every spatial position, so pruning one conv
  weight perturbs many activations. Global magnitude pruning should mostly remove FC
  weights, which buffers it, but structured channel pruning of a 16/32-channel network
  should hurt.
- *MLP:* it is heavily over-parameterized for Fashion-MNIST. Many first-layer weights
  attach to border pixels with near-constant input, so they carry little signal and should
  prune almost for free up to high sparsity.
- *Precision:* I predict INT8 costs every model < 0.5 pp of accuracy. Simulated INT4 should
  hurt the GCN and CNN more than the MLP, for the same bottleneck and weight-reuse reasons.

**Expected baseline test accuracy:** MLP about 88–89%, CNN about 90–91%, GCN about 80–81%.

"""Shared utilities: frozen environment setup, splits, run logging, code hash."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

# Repo root (project root): <root>/code/lab3/util.py -> parents[2]
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DATA_DIR = ROOT / "data"
SPLITS_DIR = ROOT / "splits"
CHECKPOINTS_DIR = ROOT / "checkpoints" / "dense"
RESULTS_DIR = ROOT / "results"
CURVES_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "curves"
RUNS_JSONL = RESULTS_DIR / "runs.jsonl"
FIGURES_DIR = ROOT / "figures"
CONFIGS_DIR = ROOT / "configs"

SPLIT_SEED = 12345
SPLIT_FILES = {
    "fmnist": [
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy",
    ],
    "cora": [
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy",
    ],
}
SPLITS_SHA = SPLITS_DIR / "SPLITS.sha256"


def set_threads() -> None:
    """Frozen thread protocol: 4 intra-op threads, 1 inter-op thread."""
    torch.set_num_threads(4)
    try:
        torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)
    except RuntimeError:
        # interop thread count can only be set before any parallel region starts
        pass


def set_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    """Frozen seed protocol: Python random, NumPy, and PyTorch."""
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)


def _sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def compute_splits_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over the six split index files (fixed order, name + array bytes)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for key in ("fmnist", "cora"):
        for path in SPLIT_FILES[key]:
            h.update(path.name.encode("utf-8"))
            h.update(_sha256_file(path).encode("ascii"))
    return h.hexdigest()


def verify_splits() -> None:
    """Load all split files and verify SPLITS.sha256; never regenerates."""
    if not SPLITS_SHA.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{SPLITS_SHA} not found. Run `uv run python -m lab3 make-splits` first. "
            "Splits are never regenerated automatically."
        )
    for key in SPLIT_FILES:
        for path in SPLIT_FILES[key]:
            if not path.exists():
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing split file {path}; run make-splits first")
    recorded = SPLITS_SHA.read_text().strip().split()[0]
    actual = compute_splits_hash()
    if actual != recorded:
        raise ValueError(
            f"split hash mismatch: recorded {recorded} != actual {actual}. "
            "Refusing to continue; run make-splits only if you intentionally reset splits."
        )


def load_indices(name: str) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    verify_splits()
    out = {}
    files = {"train": SPLIT_FILES[name][0], "val": SPLIT_FILES[name][1], "test": SPLIT_FILES[name][2]}
    for k, p in files.items():
        out[k] = np.load(p)
    return out


def code_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over all files under code/ (git-free: pure file-content hash)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    code_dir = ROOT / "code"
    for path in sorted(code_dir.rglob("*")):
        if path.is_file():
            h.update(str(path.relative_to(code_dir)).encode("utf-8"))
            h.update(path.read_bytes())
    return h.hexdigest()


def _ensure_dirs() -> None:
    for d in (DATA_DIR, SPLITS_DIR, CHECKPOINTS_DIR, RESULTS_DIR, CURVES_DIR, FIGURES_DIR):
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def new_run_id(architecture: str, method: str = "dense") -> str:
    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ")
    return f"{architecture}-{method}-{ts}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"


def write_run_record(rec: dict) -> None:
    """Append one JSON line to results/runs.jsonl. Never rewrites or deletes."""
    _ensure_dirs()
    with open(RUNS_JSONL, "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec, default=str) + "\n")
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())


def versions() -> dict:
    import platform

    return {
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "torch": torch.__version__,
        "numpy": np.__version__,
        "platform": platform.platform(),
    }


def base_record(architecture: str, command: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "run_id": new_run_id(architecture),
        "status": "ok",
        "reason": None,
        "part": "A",
        "architecture": architecture,
        "method": "dense",
        "target_sparsity": 0.0,
        "achieved_sparsity": 0.0,
        "stored_precision": "fp32",
        "compute_precision": "fp32",
        "accumulator_precision": "fp32",
        "seed": None,
        "train_epochs": None,
        "finetune_epochs": 0,
        "best_epoch": None,
        "val_acc": None,
        "val_loss": None,
        "test_acc": None,
        "total_params": None,
        "nonzero_params": None,
        "dense_bytes": None,
        "compressed_bytes": None,
        "est_macs": None,
        "peak_rss_bytes": None,
        "latency": {},
        "wall_time_s": None,
        "code_hash": code_hash(),
        "versions": versions(),
        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "command": command,
    }


def finalize_record(rec: dict, *, status: str | None = None, reason: str | None = None) -> dict:
    if status is not None:
        rec["status"] = status
        rec["reason"] = reason
    return rec


def run_wall_timer(rec: dict, t0: float) -> dict:
    rec["wall_time_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)
    return rec

def _fmnist_dataset(mode: str) -> tv_datasets.FashionMNIST:

def fmnist_split_tensors():
    """Return (train_x, train_y, val_x, val_y, test_x, test_y, mean, std) as float32
    tensors. Normalization mean/std computed on the 55k training split only (frozen).
    Indices come from the verified split files."""
    set_threads()
    idx = load_indices("fmnist")
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    test_ds = _fmnist_dataset("test")
    # 60k train and 10k test are stored as raw files; reading by index.
    tr_x = torch.stack(
        [torch.from_numpy(np.array(train_ds[int(i]))).view(1, 28, 28) for i in idx["train"]]
    ).float()
    tr_y = torch.tensor([train_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["train"]], dtype=torch.long)
    va_x = torch.stack(
        [torch.from_numpy(np.array(train_ds[int(i)])).view(1, 28, 28) for i in idx["val"]]
    ).float()
    va_y = torch.tensor([train_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["val"]], dtype=torch.long)
    te_x = torch.stack(
        [torch.from_numpy(np.array(test_ds[int(i)])).view(1, 28, 28) for i in idx["test"]]
    ).float()
    te_y = torch.tensor([test_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["test"]], dtype=torch.long)
    # Frozen: mean/std on the 55k training split only
    mean = tr_x.mean(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    std = tr_x.std(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    tr_x = (tr_x - mean) / std
    va_x = (va_x - mean) / std
    te_x = (te_x - mean) / std
    return tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, mean, std


def fmnist_norm() -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """(mean, std) computed on the 55k training split only (frozen)."""
    idx = load_indices("fmnist")
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    tr_x = torch.stack(
        [torch.from_numpy(np.array(train_ds[int(i)])).view(1, 28, 28) for i in idx["train"]]
    ).float()
    mean = tr_x.mean(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    std = tr_x.std(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    return mean, std


def fmnist_tensor_at(x: torch.Tensor, mean: torch.Tensor, std: torch.Tensor):
    return (x - mean) / std


def load_cora():
    """Load Cora (Planetoid public split) and apply the frozen preprocessing:
    row-normalized features (x / (rowsum + 1e-12)). Returns a Data object with
    float32 features, split masks, and verified node indices."""

    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid
    from torch_geometric.transforms import NormalizeFeatures

    row_sum = x.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    data.x = x / (row_sum + 1e-12)
    data.x = data.x.to(torch.float32)

    data.lm_val = torch.tensor(idx["val"], dtype=torch.long)
    data.lm_test = torch.tensor(idx["test"], dtype=torch.long)
    return data

"""Frozen training loop with validation-selected checkpointing (Part A.1)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .models import build_model, count_params, dense_bytes
from .util import (
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR,
    CURVES_DIR,
    RESULTS_DIR,
    base_record,
    new_run_id,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_seed,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)


def _eval_fmnist(model, x, y, batch_size=1024) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Validation/test evaluation on Fashion-MNIST. Eval mode only; no weight updates."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        n = len(y)
        correct = 0
        loss_sum = 0.0
        for i in range(0, n, batch_size):
            xb, yb = x[i:i + batch_size], y[i:i + batch_size]
            out = model(xb)
            loss_sum += float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb, reduction="sum").item())
            correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
    return correct / n, loss_sum / n


def _eval_cora(model, data, mask) -> tuple[float, float]:
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
        out = out[mask]
        y = data.y[mask]
        loss = float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, y).item())
        acc = float((out.argmax(dim=1) == y).float().mean().item())
    return acc, loss


def _checkpoint_path(architecture: str, seed: int):
    return CHECKPOINTS_DIR / f"{architecture}_seed{seed}.pt"


def _is_best(cand: tuple, best: tuple | None) -> bool:
    """cand=(val_acc, val_loss, epoch). Higher acc wins; tie -> lower loss; tie -> earlier epoch."""
    if best is None:
        return True
    ca, cl, ce = cand
    ba, bl, be = best
    if ca > ba:
        return True
    if ca == ba and cl < bl:
        return True
    if ca == ba and cl == bl and ce < be:
        return True
    return False


def _save_curve(run_id: str, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    CURVES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = CURVES_DIR / f"{run_id}.csv"
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=rows[0].keys())
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def train(architecture: str, cfg: dict, seed: int, run_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Frozen training protocol. Returns the run record (also appended to runs.jsonl)."""
    set_threads()
    set_seed(seed)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="train")
    rec["run_id"] = run_id or new_run_id(architecture)
    rec["seed"] = seed
    curve_rows: list[dict] = []

    try:
        model = build_model(architecture)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)

        if architecture == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            train_idx, val_idx, test_idx = data.lm_train, data.lm_val, data.lm_test
            max_epochs = int(cfg["max_epochs"])
            patience = int(cfg["patience"])
            opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
                                   weight_decay=float(cfg["weight_decay"]))

            best: tuple | None = None
            best_state: dict | None = None
            epochs_no_improve = 0
            epochs_trained = 0
            for epoch in range(1, max_epochs + 1):
                model.train()
                opt.zero_grad()
                out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
                loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(out[train_idx], data.y[train_idx])
                loss.backward()
                opt.step()
                epochs_trained = epoch

                va_acc, va_loss = _eval_cora(model, data, val_idx)
                curve_rows.append({"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": float(loss.item()),
                                   "val_acc": va_acc, "val_loss": va_loss})
                if _is_best((va_acc, va_loss, epoch), best):
                    best = (va_acc, va_loss, epoch)
                    best_state = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
                    epochs_no_improve = 0
                else:
                    epochs_no_improve += 1
                if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
                    break

            rec["train_epochs"] = epochs_trained
            rec["best_epoch"] = best[2]
            rec["val_acc"] = best[0]
            rec["val_loss"] = best[1]
            # Test set evaluated only on the selected checkpoint
            model.load_state_dict(best_state)
            te_acc, _ = _eval_cora(model, data, test_idx)
            rec["test_acc"] = te_acc
            _save_checkpoint(architecture, seed, model, rec, cfg)
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, mean, std = fmnist_split_tensors()
            batch_size = int(cfg["batch_size"])
            max_epochs = int(cfg["max_epochs"])
            patience = int(cfg["patience"])
            opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
                                   weight_decay=float(cfg["weight_decay"]))
            loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(tr_x, tr_y), batch_size=batch_size,
                                shuffle=True, drop_last=False)

            best = None
            best_state = None
            epochs_no_improve = 0
            epochs_trained = 0
            for epoch in range(1, max_epochs + 1):
                model.train()
                correct = 0
                loss_sum = 0.0
                n = 0
                for xb, yb in loader:
                    opt.zero_grad()
                    out = model(xb)
                    loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb)
                    loss.backward()
                    opt.step()
                    loss_sum += float(loss.item()) * len(yb)
                    correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
                    n += len(yb)
                epochs_trained = epoch
                va_acc, va_loss = _eval_fmnist(model, va_x, va_y)
                curve_rows.append({"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": loss_sum / n,
                                   "train_acc": correct / n,
                                   "val_acc": va_acc, "val_loss": va_loss})
                if _is_best((va_acc, va_loss, epoch), best):
                    best = (va_acc, va_loss, epoch)
                    best_state = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
                    epochs_no_improve = 0
                else:
                    epochs_no_improve += 1
                if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
                    break

            rec["train_epochs"] = epochs_trained
            rec["best_epoch"] = best[2]
            rec["val_acc"] = best[0]
            rec["val_loss"] = best[1]
            model.load_state_dict(best_state)
            te_acc, _ = _eval_fmnist(model, te_x, te_y)
            rec["test_acc"] = te_acc
            _save_checkpoint(architecture, seed, model, rec, cfg)

        _save_curve(rec["run_id"], curve_rows)
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec

    except Exception as e:  # record crashes; never leave runs.jsonl silent
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        try:
            if curve_rows:
                _save_curve(rec["run_id"], curve_rows)
        except Exception:
            pass
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise


def _save_checkpoint(architecture: str, seed: int, model, rec: dict, cfg: dict) -> None:
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    model.eval()
    torch.save({
        "state_dict": {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()},
        "metadata": {
            "architecture": architecture,
            "seed": seed,
            "best_epoch": rec["best_epoch"],
            "train_epochs": rec["train_epochs"],
            "val_acc": rec["val_acc"],
            "val_loss": rec["val_loss"],
            "test_acc": rec["test_acc"],
            "config": cfg,
            "run_id": rec["run_id"],
            "total_params": rec["total_params"],
            "dense_bytes": rec["dense_bytes"],
            "code_hash": rec["code_hash"],
            "versions": rec["versions"],
            "timestamp": rec["timestamp"],
        },
    }, _checkpoint_path(architecture, seed))

        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no checkpoint at {path}; run train first")
    payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    model = build_model(architecture)
    model.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
    return model, payload["metadata"]


def eval(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Evaluate the saved seed checkpoint on val+test. Never updates weights:
    inference_mode + eval() only. Appends a run record."""
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="eval")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")
        rec["val_loss"] = meta.get("val_loss")

        if architecture == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
                va = out[data.lm_val]
                te = out[data.lm_test]
                rec["val_loss"] = float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(va, data.y[data.lm_val]).item())
                rec["val_acc"] = float((va.argmax(dim=1) == data.y[data.lm_val]).float().mean().item())
                rec["test_acc"] = float((te.argmax(dim=1) == data.y[data.lm_test]).float().mean().item())
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for x, y, kind in ((va_x, va_y, "val"), (te_x, te_y, "test")):
                    n = len(y)
                    correct = 0
                    loss_sum = 0.0
                    bs = 1024
                    for i in range(0, n, bs):
                        xb, yb = x[i:i + bs], y[i:i + bs]
                        out = model(xb)
                        loss_sum += float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb, reduction="sum").item())
                        correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
                    if kind == "val":
                        rec["val_acc"] = correct / n
                        rec["val_loss"] = loss_sum / n
                    else:
                        rec["test_acc"] = correct / n

        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"

"""Frozen latency protocol (Part A.1) + analytical MAC estimates.

Latency: torch.inference_mode(), model in eval(). 20 warm-up and 200 timed
iterations, time.perf_counter_ns. Report median and IQR (q3 - q1).
Batch sizes 1 and 256 for Fashion-MNIST; one full-graph forward for Cora.
Peak RSS is measured in a fresh subprocess per benchmark.

MAC counting convention (analytical, per layer):
- Linear(in, out):   in * out (weights; bias excluded)
- Conv2d(cin, cout, k): cin * cout * k^2 (per output pixel)
  per image: cin * cout * k^2 * H_out * W_out
- MaxPool: 0 (no parameters, no multiplications in this convention)
- ReLU: 0
- GCNConv(in, out) with num_edges E directed edges:
  y = D_out^{-1/2} A' W D_in^{-1/2} X  (A' = A + I, self-loops added by GCNConv)
  The forward computes W @ x for every directed edge including self-loops:
    E_selfloop = E + N   (N nodes, one self-loop each)
    MACs = in * out * (E + N)   [projection W applied per (edge, feature)]
  The degree-normalization factors D^{-1/2} are elementwise scales and add
  multiplications on the order of out * (E+N); they are counted separately as
  out * (E + N) * 2 (one scale multiplication per input node and per output
  node) and are reported under the same est_macs total.

For Cora: E = 10,556, N = 2,708.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .evaln import load_checkpoint
from .models import count_params, dense_bytes
from .util import (
    RESULTS_DIR,
    base_record,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_seed,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)

WARMUP = 20
TIMED = 200
BATCH_SIZES = [1, 256]


def _macs_fmnist(architecture: str) -> int:
    if architecture == "mlp":
        return 784 * 256 + 256 * 128 + 128 * 10
    if architecture == "cnn":
        # conv1: 1*16*25 * 28*28 ; conv2: 16*32*25 * 12*12 ; fc1: 800*128 ; fc2: 128*10
        return 1 * 16 * 25 * 28 * 28 + 16 * 32 * 25 * 12 * 12 + 800 * 128 + 128 * 10
    raise ValueError(architecture)


def _macs_gcn() -> int:
    # GCNConv(in,out): in*out*(E+N) per conv; normalization: 2 * out * (E+N)
    E, N = 10556, 2708
    c1 = 1433 * 16 * (E + N)
    c2 = 16 * 7 * (E + N)
    norm = 2 * (16 + 7) * (E + N)
    return c1 + c2 + norm


def _time_batch(model, x, batch_size: int) -> dict:
    model.eval()
    idx = torch.randint(0, len(x), (WARMUP + TIMED, batch_size))
    xs = x[idx]
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for i in range(WARMUP):
            model(xs[i:i + batch_size])
        ns = []
        for i in range(TIMED):
            t0 = time.perf_counter_ns()
            model(xs[i:i + batch_size])
            ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t0)
    ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
    q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
    return {"median_ms": float(q2), "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1)}


def _bench_peak_rss(architecture: str, seed: int) -> int:
    """Peak RSS (bytes) of a fresh subprocess that loads the checkpoint, does one
    warm-up forward pass, and exits. Uses resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) ru_maxrss."""
    code = f"""
import resource
import torch
from lab3.util import set_threads
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
from lab3.data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
set_threads()
m, _ = load_checkpoint("{architecture}", {seed})
m.eval()
if "{architecture}" == "gcn":
    data = load_cora()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        m(data.x, data.edge_index)
else:
    tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        m(tr_x[:256])
rss = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
# macOS reports ru_maxrss in bytes
print(rss)
"""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=str(__import__("lab3.util", fromlist=["ROOT"]).ROOT),
    )
    return int(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])


def bench(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="bench")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")

        if architecture == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            model.eval()
            x = data.x
            ei = data.edge_index
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for _ in range(WARMUP):
                    model(x, ei)
                ns = []
                for _ in range(TIMED):
                    t_start = time.perf_counter_ns()
                    model(x, ei)
                    ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t_start)
            ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
            q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
            rec["latency"] = {
                "full_graph": {
                    "median_ms": float(q2),
                    "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1),
                    "warmup": WARMUP,
                    "iters": TIMED,
                    "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                    "batch_size": "full_graph",
                }
            }
            rec["est_macs"] = _macs_gcn()
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
            lat = {}
            for bs in BATCH_SIZES:
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"] = _time_batch(model, tr_x, bs)
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"].update({"warmup": WARMUP, "iters": TIMED,
                                           "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                                           "batch_size": bs})
            rec["latency"] = lat
            rec["est_macs"] = _macs_fmnist(architecture)

        rec["peak_rss_bytes"] = _bench_peak_rss(architecture, seed)
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise

"""CLI for the Lab 3 dense-reference package.

Usage: uv run python -m lab3 <cmd> --model {mlp,cnn,gcn} ...
Commands: make-splits, train, eval, bench.
Configs live in configs/<model>.yaml and hold the frozen hyperparameters.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import yaml
import torch

from .util import (
    CONFIGS_DIR,
    DATA_DIR,
    SPLIT_SEED,
    SPLITS_DIR,
    compute_splits_hash,
    set_threads,
)


def load_config(architecture: str) -> dict:
    path = CONFIGS_DIR / f"{architecture}.yaml"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing config {path}")
    with open(path) as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f)


def make_splits() -> None:
    """Create the frozen splits exactly once. Refuses to overwrite existing files."""
    set_threads()
    existing = [p for key in ("fmnist", "cora") for p in [
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy", SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy", SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy", SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "SPLITS.sha256"]]
    if any(p.exists() for p in existing):
        raise FileExistsError("splits already exist; refusing to regenerate. "
                              "Delete splits/ manually only if you intend to reset all arms.")
    SPLITS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(SPLIT_SEED)

    # --- Fashion-MNIST: stratified 5000 (500/class) val from the 60k train ---
    from .data import _fmnist_dataset
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    labels = np.asarray(train_ds.targets)
    assert labels.shape[0] == 60000
    val_idx = []
    for cls in range(10):
        pool = np.flatnonzero(labels == cls)
        chosen = np.random.permutation(pool)[:500]
        val_idx.append(chosen)
    val_idx = np.sort(np.concatenate(val_idx))
    train_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(60000), val_idx, assume_unique=True)
    test_idx = np.arange(10000)
    assert train_idx.shape[0] == 55000 and val_idx.shape[0] == 5000

    np.save(SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy", train_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy", val_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy", test_idx.astype(np.int64))

    # --- Cora: standard Planetoid public split ---
    from .data import load_cora
    data = load_cora()  # verifies nothing yet; but cora split files needed... see below
    # NOTE: load_cora verifies splits, which we are creating now. To avoid the
    # chicken-and-egg, load the dataset directly here.
    raise RuntimeError("unreachable")


def _cora_masks():
    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid
    from .util import DATA_DIR as _D
    ds = Planetoid(root=str(_D / "Planetoid"), name="Cora")
    g = ds[0]
    return g.train_mask, g.val_mask, g.test_mask


def make_splits_impl() -> None:
    set_threads()
    import lab3.util as U
    existing = [p for p in U.SPLIT_FILES["fmnist"] + U.SPLIT_FILES["cora"] + [U.SPLITS_SHA]]
    if any(p.exists() for p in existing):
        raise FileExistsError("splits already exist; refusing to regenerate. "
                              "Delete splits/ manually only if you intend to reset all arms.")
    U.SPLITS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(SPLIT_SEED)

    from .data import _fmnist_dataset
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    labels = np.asarray(train_ds.targets)
    assert labels.shape[0] == 60000
    val_idx = []
    for cls in range(10):
        pool = np.flatnonzero(labels == cls)
        val_idx.append(np.random.permutation(pool)[:500])
    val_idx = np.sort(np.concatenate(val_idx))
    train_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(60000), val_idx, assume_unique=True)
    test_idx = np.arange(10000)
    assert train_idx.shape[0] == 55000 and val_idx.shape[0] == 5000

    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy", train_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy", val_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy", test_idx.astype(np.int64))

    tr_m, va_m, te_m = _cora_masks()
    cora_tr = np.flatnonzero(tr_m.numpy())
    cora_va = np.flatnonzero(va_m.numpy())
    cora_te = np.flatnonzero(te_m.numpy())
    assert cora_tr.shape[0] == 140 and cora_va.shape[0] == 500 and cora_te.shape[0] == 1000
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy", cora_tr.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy", cora_va.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy", cora_te.astype(np.int64))

    U.SPLITS_SHA.write_text(compute_splits_hash() + "  splits/*.npy (fixed order, see compute_splits_hash)\n")
    print(f"splits written to {U.SPLITS_DIR}; hash={compute_splits_hash()}")


def _apply_overrides(cfg: dict, args) -> dict:
    """CLI flags override frozen config values (for tests only)."""
    for flag, key in (("--lr", "lr"), ("--weight-decay", "weight_decay"),
                      ("--batch-size", "batch_size"), ("--epochs", "max_epochs"),
                      ("--patience", "patience")):
        val = getattr(args, flag.replace("-", "_"), None)
        if val is not None:
            cfg[key] = val
    return cfg


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="lab3")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("make-splits")
    p.set_defaults(fn=make_splits_impl)

    for name, help_ in (("train", "train a dense model"),
                        ("eval", "evaluate a saved checkpoint"),
                        ("bench", "benchmark a saved checkpoint")):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=help_)
        p.add_argument("--model", required=True, choices=["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
        p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
        p.add_argument("--run-id", default=None)
        # overrides (tests only)
        p.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--weight-decay", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--patience", type=int, default=None)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    set_threads()

    if args.cmd == "make-splits":
        args.fn()
        return 0

    cfg = load_config(args.model)
    cfg = _apply_overrides(cfg, args)

    if args.cmd == "train":
        from .training import train
        rec = train(args.model, cfg, seed=args.seed, run_id=args.run_id)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} best_epoch={rec['best_epoch']} "
              f"val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f} "
              f"epochs={rec['train_epochs']} wall={rec['wall_time_s']}s")
    elif args.cmd == "eval":
        from .evaln import eval as do_eval
        rec = do_eval(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f}")
    elif args.cmd == "bench":
        from .bench import bench
        rec = bench(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        lat = rec["latency"]
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} latency={lat} peak_rss={rec['peak_rss_bytes']}B")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""CLI for the Lab 3 dense-reference package.

Usage: uv run python -m lab3 <cmd> --model {mlp,cnn,gcn} ...
Commands: make-splits, train, eval, bench.
Configs live in configs/<model>.yaml and hold the frozen hyperparameters.
CLI flags may override config values for tests only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import yaml
import torch

from .util import (
    CONFIGS_DIR,
    DATA_DIR,
    SPLIT_SEED,
    SPLITS_DIR,
    compute_splits_hash,
    set_threads,
)


def load_config(architecture: str) -> dict:
    path = CONFIGS_DIR / f"{architecture}.yaml"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing config {path}")
    with open(path) as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f)


def main:
    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid
    from .util import DATA_DIR as _D
    ds = Planetoid(root=str(_D / "Planetoid"), name="Cora")
    g = ds[0]
    return g.train_mask, g.val_mask, g.test_mask


def make_splits_impl() -> None:
    set_threads()
    import lab3.util as U
    existing = [p for p in U.SPLIT_FILES["fmnist"] + U.SPLIT_FILES["cora"] + [U.SPLITS_SHA]]
    if any(p.exists() for p in existing):
        raise FileExistsError("splits already exist; refusing to regenerate. "
                              "Delete splits/ manually only if you intend to reset all arms.")
    U.SPLITS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(SPLIT_SEED)

    from .data import _fmnist_dataset
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    labels = np.asarray(train_ds.targets)
    assert labels.shape[0] == 60000
    val_idx = []
    for cls in range(10):
        pool = np.flatnonzero(labels == cls)
        val_idx.append(np.random.permutation(pool)[:500])
    val_idx = np.sort(np.concatenate(val_idx))
    train_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(60000), val_idx, assume_unique=True)
    test_idx = np.arange(10000)
    assert train_idx.shape[0] == 55000 and val_idx.shape[0] == 5000

    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy", train_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy", val_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy", test_idx.astype(np.int64))

    tr_m, va_m, te_m = _cora_masks()
    cora_tr = np.flatnonzero(tr_m.numpy())
    cora_va = np.flatnonzero(va_m.numpy())
    cora_te = np.flatnonzero(te_m.numpy())
    assert cora_tr.shape[0] == 140 and cora_va.shape[0] == 500 and cora_te.shape[0] == 1000
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy", cora_tr.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy", cora_va.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy", cora_te.astype(np.int64))

    U.SPLITS_SHA.write_text(compute_splits_hash() + "  splits/*.npy (fixed order, see compute_splits_hash)\n")
    print(f"splits written to {U.SPLITS_DIR}; hash={compute_splits_hash()}")


def _apply_overrides(cfg: dict, args) -> dict:
    """CLI flags override frozen config values (for tests only)."""
    for flag, key in (("--lr", "lr"), ("--weight-decay", "weight_decay"),
                      ("--batch-size", "batch_size"), ("--epochs", "max_epochs"),
                      ("--patience", "patience")):
        val = getattr(args, flag.replace("-", "_"), None)
        if val is not None:
            cfg[key] = val
    return cfg


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="lab3")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("make-splits")
    p.set_defaults(fn=make_splits_impl)

    for name, help_ in (("train", "train a dense model"),
                        ("eval", "evaluate a saved checkpoint"),
                        ("bench", "benchmark a saved checkpoint")):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=help_)
        p.add_argument("--model", required=True, choices=["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
        p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
        p.add_argument("--run-id", default=None)
        # overrides (tests only)
        p.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--weight-decay", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--patience", type=int, default=None)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    set_threads()

    if args.cmd == "make-splits":
        args.fn()
        return 0

    cfg = load_config(args.model)
    cfg = _apply_overrides(cfg, args)

    if args.cmd == "train":
        from .training import train
        rec = train(args.model, cfg, seed=args.seed, run_id=args.run_id)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} best_epoch={rec['best_epoch']} "
              f"val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f} "
              f"epochs={rec['train_epochs']} wall={rec['wall_time_s']}s")
    elif args.cmd == "eval":
        from .evaln import eval as do_eval
        rec = do_eval(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f}")
    elif args.cmd == "bench":
        from .bench import bench
        rec = bench(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        lat = rec["latency"]
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} latency={lat} peak_rss={rec['peak_rss_bytes']}B")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Test (c): evaluation never updates weights — state_dict bit-identical and
optimizer untouched after `eval` and after `bench`."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from lab3.models import build_model
from lab3.data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from lab3.util import set_threads


def _snapshot(model: nn.Module) -> dict:
    return {k: v.clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}


def _assert_bit_identical(before: dict, after_model: nn.Module) -> None:
    after = after_model.state_dict()
    assert set(before) == set(after)
    for k in before:
        b, a = before[k], after[k]
        assert b.dtype == a.dtype
        assert torch.equal(b.view(torch.uint8), a.view(torch.uint8)), f"tensor {k} changed"


def _fmnist_pair(arch: str):
    model = build_model(arch)
    model.eval()
    tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
    return model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y


def _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y):
    """Replicates the weight-relevant part of lab3.evaln.eval (inference_mode, eval)."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for x, y in ((va_x, va_y), (te_x, te_y)):
            n = len(y)
            for i in range(0, n, 1024):
                nn.functional.cross_entropy(model(x[i:i + 1024]), y[i:i + 1024])


def test_eval_never_updates_mlp():
    set_threads()
    model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y = _fmnist_pair("mlp")
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    opt.state = {}  # untouched baseline
    before = _snapshot(model)
    from lab3.evaln import eval as do_eval  # noqa: F401 (import check)
    _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y)
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)
    assert opt.state == {}


def test_eval_never_updates_cnn():
    set_threads()
    model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y = _fmnist_pair("cnn")
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y)
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)
    assert opt.state == {}


def test_eval_never_updates_gcn():

    model = build_model("gcn")
    data = load_cora()
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, weight_decay=5e-4)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
        nn.functional.cross_entropy(out[data.lm_val], data.y[data.lm_val])
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)

"""Data loading: Fashion-MNIST and Cora (Planetoid public split)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import torch
from torchvision import datasets as tv_datasets


def _fmnist_dataset(mode: str) -> tv_datasets.FashionMNIST:
    """mode in {'train','test'}: official 60k/10k sets, raw uint8 pixels."""
    from .util import DATA_DIR

    return tv_datasets.FashionMNIST(
        root=str(DATA_DIR), train=(mode == "train"), download=True
    )


def _images(ds: tv_datasets.FashionMNIST, idx: np.ndarray) -> torch.Tensor:
    """(N,1,28,28) float32 tensor for the given indices (raw 0..255)."""
    out = torch.empty((len(idx), 1, 28, 28), dtype=torch.float32)
    for row, i in enumerate(idx):
        out[row] = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(ds[int(i)])).view(1, 28, 28)
    return out


def fmnist_split_tensors():
    """Return (train_x, train_y, val_x, val_y, test_x, test_y, mean, std) as float32
    tensors. Normalization mean/std computed on the 55k training split only (frozen).
    Indices come from the verified split files."""
    from .util import load_indices, set_threads

    set_threads()
    idx = load_indices("fmnist")
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    test_ds = _fmnist_dataset("test")
    tr_x = _images(train_ds, idx["train"])
    tr_y = torch.tensor([train_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["train"]], dtype=torch.long)
    va_x = _images(train_ds, idx["val"])
    va_y = torch.tensor([train_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["val"]], dtype=torch.long)
    te_x = _images(test_ds, idx["test"])
    te_y = torch.tensor([test_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["test"]], dtype=torch.long)
    # Frozen: mean/std on the 55k training split only
    mean = tr_x.mean(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    std = tr_x.std(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    tr_x = (tr_x - mean) / std
    va_x = (va_x - mean) / std
    te_x = (te_x - mean) / std
    return tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, mean, std


def load_cora():
    """Load Cora (Planetoid public split) and apply the frozen preprocessing:
    row-normalized features (x / (rowsum + 1e-12)). Returns a Data object with
    float32 features and the verified node index tensors lm_train/lm_val/lm_test."""
    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid

    from .util import DATA_DIR, load_indices, set_threads

    set_threads()
    dataset = Planetoid(root=str(DATA_DIR / "Planetoid"), name="Cora")
    data = dataset[0]

    # Frozen: Cora features row-normalized (standard GCN preprocessing).
    x = data.x
    row_sum = x.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    data.x = (x / (row_sum + 1e-12)).to(torch.float32)

    idx = load_indices("cora")
    data.lm_train = torch.tensor(idx["train"], dtype=torch.long)
    data.lm_val = torch.tensor(idx["val"], dtype=torch.long)
    data.lm_test = torch.tensor(idx["test"], dtype=torch.long)
    return data

"""Test (c): evaluation never updates weights — state_dict bit-identical and
optimizer untouched after `eval` and after `bench`."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from lab3.models import build_model
from lab3.data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from lab3.util import set_threads
from test_splits import _make_splits_once


def _snapshot(model: nn.Module) -> dict:
    return {k: v.clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}


def _assert_bit_identical(before: dict, after_model: nn.Module) -> None:
    after = after_model.state_dict()
    assert set(before) == set(after)
    for k in before:
        b, a = before[k], after[k]
        assert b.dtype == a.dtype
        assert torch.equal(b.view(torch.uint8), a.view(torch.uint8)), f"tensor {k} changed"


def _fmnist_pair(arch: str):
    model = build_model(arch)
    model.eval()
    _make_splits_once()
    tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
    return model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y


def _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y):
    """Replicates the weight-relevant part of lab3.evaln.eval (inference_mode, eval)."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for x, y in ((va_x, va_y), (te_x, te_y)):
            n = len(y)
            for i in range(0, n, 1024):
                nn.functional.cross_entropy(model(x[i:i + 1024]), y[i:i + 1024])


def test_eval_never_updates_mlp():
    set_threads()
    model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y = _fmnist_pair("mlp")
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y)
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)
    assert opt.state == {}


def test_eval_never_updates_cnn():
    set_threads()
    model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y = _fmnist_pair("cnn")
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y)
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)
    assert opt.state == {}


def test_eval_never_updates_gcn():
    set_threads()
    _make_splits_once()
    model = build_model("gcn")
    data = load_cora()
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, weight_decay=5e-4)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
        nn.functional.cross_entropy(out[data.lm_val], data.y[data.lm_val])
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)
    assert opt.state == {}


def test_bench_forward_never_updates():
    """The bench timing loop is a plain inference_mode forward pass; verify it
    cannot mutate any parameter, for all three architectures."""
    set_threads()
    _make_splits_once()
    for arch in ("mlp", "cnn", "gcn"):
        model = build_model(arch)
        opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
        before = _snapshot(model)
        if arch == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                model(data.x, data.edge_index)
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                model(tr_x[:256])
        _assert_bit_identical(before, model)
        assert opt.state == {}

"""Test (d): split files load, hashes match, splits are disjoint, fmnist val
is 500 per class. Creates the session's real split files if missing (same
frozen procedure as make-splits, split seed 12345)."""
import numpy as np

import lab3.util as U
from lab3.util import load_indices, verify_splits, SPLIT_SEED


def _make_splits_once():
    """Create the session's real split files if missing (tests need them)."""
    existing = [p for p in U.SPLIT_FILES["fmnist"] + U.SPLIT_FILES["cora"] + [U.SPLITS_SHA]]
    if all(p.exists() for p in existing):
        return
    U.SPLITS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(SPLIT_SEED)

    from lab3.data import _fmnist_dataset
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    labels = np.asarray(train_ds.targets)
    val_idx = []
    for cls in range(10):
        pool = np.flatnonzero(labels == cls)
        val_idx.append(np.random.permutation(pool)[:500])
    val_idx = np.sort(np.concatenate(val_idx))
    train_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(60000), val_idx, assume_unique=True)
    test_idx = np.arange(10000)

    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy", train_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy", val_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy", test_idx.astype(np.int64))

    from lab3.cli import _cora_masks
    tr_m, va_m, te_m = _cora_masks()
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy", np.flatnonzero(tr_m.numpy()).astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy", np.flatnonzero(va_m.numpy()).astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy", np.flatnonzero(te_m.numpy()).astype(np.int64))

    U.SPLITS_SHA.write_text(U.compute_splits_hash() + "\n")


def test_split_files_load_and_hash():
    _make_splits_once()
    verify_splits()
    fm = load_indices("fmnist")
    co = load_indices("cora")
    assert fm["train"].shape[0] == 55000
    assert fm["val"].shape[0] == 5000
    assert fm["test"].shape[0] == 10000
    assert co["train"].shape[0] == 140
    assert co["val"].shape[0] == 500
    assert co["test"].shape[0] == 1000


def test_splits_disjoint():
    """Within-dataset disjointness. Note: fmnist train/val are indices into the
    60k train set while fmnist test indices refer to the separate 10k test set,
    so cross-set index overlap is by design and not checked."""
    _make_splits_once()
    fm = load_indices("fmnist")
    co = load_indices("cora")
    # fmnist: train and val both index the 60k train pool -> must be disjoint
    # and together cover all 60k train images exactly once.
    t, v = fm["train"], fm["val"]
    assert len(np.intersect1d(t, v)) == 0, "fmnist train/val overlap"
    union = np.union1d(t, v)
    assert union.shape[0] == 60000 and union.min() == 0 and union.max() == 59999
    assert np.array_equal(np.sort(np.concatenate([t, v])), np.arange(60000))
    # fmnist test: official 10k set
    assert np.array_equal(fm["test"], np.arange(10000))
    # cora: all three index the same 2708-node graph -> pairwise disjoint
    ct, cv, cte = co["train"], co["val"], co["test"]
    assert len(np.intersect1d(ct, cv)) == 0, "cora train/val overlap"
    assert len(np.intersect1d(ct, cte)) == 0, "cora train/test overlap"
    assert len(np.intersect1d(cv, cte)) == 0, "cora val/test overlap"
    assert np.union1d(ct, np.union1d(cv, cte)).shape[0] == 1640


def test_fmnist_val_500_per_class():
    _make_splits_once()
    from lab3.data import _fmnist_dataset
    fm = load_indices("fmnist")
    labels = np.asarray(_fmnist_dataset("train").targets)
    for cls in range(10):
        assert int((labels[fm["val"]] == cls).sum()) == 500, f"val class {cls} != 500"

Apple M4 Pro, CPU only, `torch.set_num_threads(4)`, interop threads 1.
Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.15.0 / torchvision 0.29.2 / torch_geometric 2.8.1 / NumPy 2.5.4.

Seed-0 rows are the canonical dense checkpoints for the compression arms.

## Sanity targets (test acc, seed 0): all met

| model | target | seed 0 | seed mean (0-3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | ≥ 82% | **89.29%** | 89.14% |
| CNN | ≥ 87% | **90.87%** | 91.30% |
| GCN | ≥ 65% | **80.80%** | 81.40% |

## Baseline table (seed-0 canonical checkpoints)

| model | val acc (s0) | test acc (s0) | test acc seeds 1-3 | params | FP32 bytes | est. MACs | latency median (IQR) | peak RSS (fresh proc.) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | 0.8986 | 0.8929 | 0.8935 / 0.8873 / 0.8918 | 235,146 | 940,584 B (0.90 MB) | 234,752 (per image) | bs1 0.0125 ms (0.0004); bs256 0.1314 ms (0.0056) | 1.05 GB |
| CNN | 0.9182 | 0.9087 | 0.9150 / 0.9134 / 0.9147 | 117,066 | 468,264 B (0.45 MB) | 2,260,480 (per image) | bs1 0.0935 ms (0.0032); bs256 7.1090 ms (0.1033) | 1.08 GB |
| GCN | 0.8000 | 0.8080 | 0.8070 / 0.8220 / 0.8200 | 23,063 | 92,252 B (0.09 MB) | 306,212,704 (full graph) | full-graph 1.0422 ms (0.0311) | 0.39 GB |

- Latency protocol: `torch.inference_mode()`, `eval()`, 20 warm-up / 200 timed iterations,
  `time.perf_counter_ns`, median + IQR reported. Batch 1 and 256 for fmnist (pre-allocated
  fixed batch, so the timed region is the forward pass only); one full-graph forward for Cora.
- Peak RSS measured in a fresh subprocess that loads the seed-0 checkpoint, runs a few
  forward passes, and reports the max `psutil` RSS.
- MAC convention (analytical): Linear = in×out; Conv2d = cin×cout×k²×H_out×W_out per image;
  MaxPool/ReLU = 0; GCNConv(in,out) = in×out×(E+N) per conv where GCNConv adds self-loops
  (N=2,708, E=10,556), plus 2×out×(E+N) for the two degree-normalization scaling passes.
- Training (frozen): MLP/CNN Adam lr 1e-3, wd 0, bs 128, max 30 epochs, patience 5;
  GCN Adam lr 0.01, wd 5e-4, full-batch, max 300 epochs, patience 50.
  Checkpoint = best val acc (ties: lower val loss, then earlier epoch); test evaluated
  only on the selected checkpoint.
- Seed variance (test acc): MLP 88.73-89.35, CNN 90.87-91.50, GCN 80.70-82.20.

## Training stops

| model | best epoch | epochs run | stop reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | 16 | 21 | patience (no val acc improvement for 5 epochs) |
| CNN | 20 | 25 | patience |
| GCN | 93 | 143 | patience |

## Notes / anomalies

- predictions.md expected test acc ≈ MLP 88-89%, CNN 90-91%, GCN 80-81%: observed
  seed-0 values 89.29 / 90.87 / 80.80 — all inside or above the predicted ranges.
- Checkpoint file sizes on disk include zip/pickle overhead; the "FP32 bytes" column is the

- No anomalies: every run in results/runs.jsonl is status=ok (earlier failed bench lines
  are retained per the append-only log rule and are documented debugging of the bench
  protocol, superseded by the final bench runs above).
